Alicia: Heads-up — noticed a regression in TP all-reduce latency on latest runtime build when model chunking crosses 64KB per rank. latency jumps ~2.2x. I think kernel selection + packing heuristics are picking a bad path.

Tom: oof. saw anything in nvprof traces or ncu timeline? :eyes:

Alicia: grabbed a short trace on a 4xA100 TP job. main anomaly is long host-to-device memcpy stalls followed by lots of tiny NCCL sends instead of fewer larger ones. pasted the relevant snippet:

```
# ncu summary
Kernel: ncclSend/Recv - many calls (~10k), avg size 5-8KB, latency spiking
MemcpyHtoD: bursts aligned with token boundary, 1.2ms stalls
App compute overlaps ~20% only
```

Kevin: that sounds like our chunk packing heuristic is emitting micro-chunks because kvcache boundaries align with transformer KV segment size. Are we forcing chunk <= kv-entry-size anywhere?

Alicia: yes, the change in pr 2043 introduced conservative packing to avoid merging entries across attention heads. It added `max_chunk = min(cfg.chunk_limit, kv_entry_size)` which reduced worst-case correctness issues but increased comm calls.

Sam: can you repro with toggles? if you flip the old packing heuristic off does it go back to baseline?

Alicia: quick test results:
- baseline (v2042): allreduce median RTT 0.9ms
- after pr2043: 2.0ms
- after forcing `merge_across_heads=true`: 0.95ms
So it looks directly linked.

Kevin: interesting. But also check kernel selector: when chunk sizes drop below ~16KB we fallback to a 'small-msg' kernel path which disables asynchronous gather. That defeats comm/compute overlap. Maybe selector threshold tuned wrongly.

Alicia: good point — I saw the runtime log: `Picked kernel: allreduce_smallmsg_v2` repeatedly.

PerfBot: automated regression alert: tp_allreduce_latency increased by 120% in nightly-canary. Linked traces: /runs/2105/trace-2105006789.npz

Tom: proposal: 1) temporary revert conservative packing, 2) adjust kernel selection thresholds to prefer async path up to 32KB, 3) add passive coalesce step that merges consecutive kv entries when safe. Thoughts?

Kevin: +1 for passive coalesce. Revert is risky if we had correctness bug. We should craft a safe merge predicate: same head/seq, contiguous addresses, no partial-token markers. We can implement and test quickly.

Alicia: I can prototype passive coalesce in the packer today. Also will add a config flag `tp.force_kernel_async_threshold=32768` for quick experiments.

Sam: also add a perf test that exercises many small messages to avoid reintroducing regression. e.g., run the tp microbench with kv_entry_size=4KB and batch=2 for ~5k iterations.

Alicia: created a branch `tp/pack-coalesce-2105`. pushed quick changes and a perf run. link: https://git.internal/redwood/rt/compare/tp/pack-coalesce-2105

Tom: ran your perf job — initial numbers look promising: allreduce median 1.0ms with coalesce + threshold bump. but GPU utilization drop? check kernels overlapping.

Alicia: saw that too. nvprof now shows more contiguous NCCL send sizes (avg ~28KB) and fewer memcpy stalls, but app compute dropped from 40% overlap to 34% in one run — looks like packing changed timing slightly.

Kevin: acceptable if end-to-end latency improves. We should add a conservative canary: enable coalesce only for dedicated builds and run on staging to validate no correctness regressions with attention mask edgecases.

Sam: can we add an assert in dev builds that verifies round-trip kv contents after merging? cheap checksum compare before/after pack/unpack.

Alicia: yep will add checksum, and an integration test that randomizes head boundaries. Also adding a microbench harness script I used:

```
# tools/tp_perf.sh
python3 -m rwinf.bench.tp --gpus 4 --model tiny --kv-entry 4096 --batch 2 --iters 5000 --trace out.npz
```

Using that to reproduce.

PerfBot: note: schedule regression-ci run on branch `tp/pack-coalesce-2105` automatically queued.

Tom: follow-up: we should revisit kernel selection strategy long-term. current heuristics are too brittle to packing semantics. Maybe expose a dynamic probe: measure recent average msg size and override selector for next N iterations. That would make it adaptive per workload.

Kevin: yes — adaptive selector + moving average of msg size would handle bursty token distributions. We can add a sampling window and an override. I'll sketch design.

Alicia: action items I captured:
- add passive coalesce + checksum in dev (Alicia)
- config flag for async threshold + quick canary (Alicia/Tom)
- regression perf test (Sam)
- design adaptive kernel selector (Kevin)

Sam: sounds good. Ping me when canary passes and I'll roll to dedicated staging. :thumbsup:

Kevin: FYI leaving a note: this may also affect Dedicated autoscaler heuristics since smaller messages influenced CPU scheduling. keep an eye.

Alicia: will post final numbers and traces once canary finishes. thanks all. :raised_hands:
